headline: mSecure password manager hack prompts reset warnings; APT29 mobile exploit campaign and cPGuard supply chain attack stay on top

bullets.text: New, mSecure, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports a hack of the mSecure password manager has prompted password reset warnings. The Register says mSecure told users to change their passwords and would not say why.

Still active, critical: The Hacker News reports APT29-linked hackers hijacked a web analytics script to deliver iOS and Android exploits. BleepingComputer and Help Net Security describe the exploits as n-day, and BleepingComputer calls the attacks zero-click.
Still active: The Hacker News reports Google issued patches for a critical Android flaw, CVE-2026-58868, that could allow remote code execution without user interaction.

Still active, cPGuard, 4 outlets: SecurityWeek reports malicious updates served in an OpsShield supply chain attack. Help Net Security says the poisoned update hit thousands of web hosting servers, and BleepingComputer says it deployed a backdoor and stole data.

Still active, WordPress Core, 3 outlets: BleepingComputer reports CISA flags a WordPress RCE flaw as actively exploited. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-119977, a race condition added 2026-11-03, with a federal due date of 2026-11-06.

Still active, Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.

actions: If you or your staff use mSecure, change the master password and rotate the credentials stored in it, starting with the most sensitive.
Update managed iOS and Android devices to current releases, and apply Google's patch for CVE-2026-58868 as it reaches your fleet.
If you run cPGuard, check servers for the backdoor reported by BleepingComputer and treat data on affected hosts as exposed.
Update WordPress Core for CVE-2026-119977 per vendor guidance; the KEV federal due date is 2026-11-06.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
If you use WorkOS, Northflank or Trigger.dev, read their disclosures and review the access and tokens you share with them.
